blocks.content: My apartment faces east, so the light comes in before I'm ready for it. I've been here seven months and I still haven't fixed the blinds.
I've thought about why that is. The honest answer is that fixing them would mean one less thing between me and having to be awake.

I keep my space organized because I paint in it. That's the reason I give myself, anyway. The paints are sorted by temperature — warms on the left, cools on the right — and the brushes stand handle-up in mason jars, and the canvases lean against the far wall from tallest to shortest. My mom came over in April and stood in the doorway for a long moment before she asked if I was okay. I said I was. She moved one of my brushes two inches while we were talking, and I noticed the second she did it, and I didn't say anything.
I'm not sure what that says about me.

The sketchbook on the desk doesn't follow any of it. The cover has pencil smudges and a coffee ring I never cleaned because the shape of it was right — it landed at an angle that worked, and removing it felt like a decision I'd regret. The pages inside look like what the rest of the apartment doesn't: like something actually happens here.
I pulled on my running clothes. Drank half a glass of water at the sink.
